reason: Answers Murray on specimen copy, price and the £72 corrections; all points raised in the question.
Congratulates on salary/house and gives the room cost Hooker explicitly asked for.
Direct reaction to Hooker's plea about the Lyell eloge.
Responds squarely to De Candolle's begged election and Asa Gray's claims.
Answer is a receipt-of-letters acknowledgement; the Cambridge/Whewell news is answered by a different reply paragraph.
Thanks prompted by Poole's offer of replies on the Kattywar horses.
Answer text (Sinclair, De Candolle, large genera) appears nowhere in this letter's reply; wrong reply entirely.
Answer is an Asa Gray letter about his Manual and alpine plants; not the reply to Hooker's Galapagos letter.
Directly engages Hooker's India/Australia distribution facts with the N-to-S migration argument.
Thanks Ramsay and drafts the sentence using exactly the Longmynd/Laurentian facts supplied.
Covers both raised points: European species in Australia, and the seed-germination explanation he distrusts.
Answers Pallas, crossing, and Hooker's centripetal/centrifugal terms, all raised by Lyell.
Answers Gray's explicit 'is it worth while to go on at this length of detail?' with praise of the Statistics paper.
Reacts to the hermaphrodite-trees fact and asks a follow-up about Eucalyptus pollen.
Sustained reply to Hooker's 'Australian forms are highest' argument, point for point.
Answer is about man's selection vs nature's, prompted by Lyell's next paragraph, not by this one on hybrid sterility.
Answer is only the bare valediction, aligned to a substantive opening paragraph of Davy's report.
Valediction correctly paired with Higgins's valediction; trivial but genuinely prompted.
Answer on grass crossing and Papilionaceous flowers does not occur in this reply at all.
Returns the proof sheets Hooker sent and comments on the abstract; directly prompted.
Answers only the Lyell eloge request; incomplete but nothing unprompted.
Thanks for the praise, responds on the Athenaeum review and Woodward, sends regards to the Lyells, all raised.
Direct reaction to the news that Huxley may lecture.

Corrections, the eye passage, 'living' naturalists, Madeira birds and Lamarck all come from the question; only the Scarborough proof-sheet line and the Bunbury greeting bleed in from adjacent paragraphs.
Concedes Lubbock's difficulty about allied forms differing in important organs.
Rebuts exactly Lyell's Galapagos/American-type creationist argument.
Answers Lyell's objection to the multiple origin of dogs.
Second answer paragraph on continued creative intervention belongs to Lyell's later paragraphs, not the Galapagos one quoted.
Gives the rattlesnake explanation Lyell asked to be told.
Thanks Leighton for the bean specimens and for permission to use them; both in the question.
Thanks and replies to the news of Lubbock's brother; brief but genuine.
Expounds Pallas's doctrine, gestation period and races of man exactly as Lyell requested.
Responds to Hooker's remark about arriving at the refrigeration doctrine independently.
Answers the Lyellian notes and the Ralfs subscription news.
Answers Lyell's demand for continued intervention of creative power, which the quoted paragraphs make.
Concedes the Aphis error and follows up on Dufour, prompted by Lubbock's embryology note.
One-line reply to Lyell's point about migration across the tropical zone.
Settles the Beesby shooting question exactly as Higgins suggested.
Answers the MS loan, transmigration date, Australian palaeozoic plants and Chobham sands, all asked.
Full reply to Lyell on 'principle of improvement' and 'power of adaptation'.
Follow-up queries and explanations arising directly from Poole's numbered answers on dun horses and stripes.
Long rebuttal on naturalised Australian plants and the Nilgherries; only a three-word thanks for glaciers is extra.
Responds to Murray on circulating copies and the foreign ones.
Accepts Lubbock's proposed Saturday visit.
